controls.enforcement: Common command runs the real lint-imports executable and propagates failure; temporary source fixtures exercise allowed composition and direct/indirect forbidden imports.

controls.name: Design and independent change review
controls.scope: Consequential designs, implementation, tests, delegation and exceptions.
controls.mechanism: Lead owns design/integration and verifies returned evidence; at most two workers use separate project-local worktrees and named disjoint paths, with shared runtime serialized; fresh-context review assesses contracts, risk and maintainability before acceptance. Review new or expanded custom infrastructure across code/docs/workflow/controls against S-CODE: name the existing option, unmet gap, smallest scope, owner/cost and retirement trigger; reject unjustified duplication. Before publication, inspect explicit Git author/committer identities and all new commit messages, including co-author trailers, under S-WORK. Use repository-local Git identity configuration. Before merging a PR whose Issue completion awaits merged-main validation, read gh pr view --json closingIssuesReferences, require an empty list and re-read after removing references. Prose negation is not a parser control; use GitHub computed data, no custom keyword parser.
controls.trigger: significant change, new boundary/guarantee/dependency or integration checkpoint
controls.failure_response: Resolve material findings or record scoped owner/reason/revisit exception; after two unsuccessful worker repairs lead takes back the work.
controls.limitations: No code checker proves reasoning quality, typing completeness, decomposition or delegation compliance; independence depends on the actual review process. Reuse fit and the adequacy of its rationale are semantic judgments; CI does not prove them. Identity configuration prevents inferred defaults but does not inspect file contents or prove a message, branch or remote ref contains no personal information; full-message inspection remains manual.
controls.enforcement: Required by S-AGENT and the GitHub work/PR workflow; independent agent review is manually recorded, not an independent GitHub human approval. Hosted enforcement is recorded separately in acceptance.

controls.scope: Checkpoint/release scope, source provenance and validation lanes.
controls.mechanism: Inspect staged diff and candidate identity, run common checks against exact candidate, review pins/open exceptions and require relevant native probes for affected claims. Git owns tracked-source identity: commit before native acceptance and use commit/tree/diff/PR; hash external artifacts instead of maintaining per-source history.
controls.failure_response: Hold the affected acceptance/release claim until failed or unexecuted required lanes are resolved or scope is explicitly reduced.
controls.limitations: Working-tree hooks do not prove a partially staged candidate. Hosted source/check enforcement does not establish native gameplay, semantic review or release authority. No tag or release automation is installed; administrators can later change rules. GitHub requires association with an opened PR, not use of its merge button; a passing PR head can be pushed and recognized as merged. A required-PR rejection probe needs a CI-passing commit with no PR.
controls.enforcement: Main requires a PR, the Actions-bound controller check and resolved conversations; no force-push/deletion or configured bypass. Lead still owns native/release acceptance. Zero required human approvals is an explicit single-account limit; agent review is not human approval.

controls.trigger: common command; source, renderer configuration or dependency changes require rendered review
controls.failure_response: Fix syntax or missing setup; regenerate stale output and inspect the rendered result. Never call a denied browser launch a passed check. Resolve semantic/readability findings through C-USABILITY/C-REVIEW.

controls.rationale: Required to keep user-facing visual explanations reviewable and synchronized.
